All affected properties should have this documented, because emitting the signal only in the editor is an exception. 
Whether it should at project run-time as well is debatable. If anything, all other particle properties should make note that `changed` is not emitted for them, but that's for another time.

Something like `[b]Note:[/b] Only in the editor, changing this property emits the [signal Resource.changed] signal`.
Done as suggested 👍🏻 The signal is only emitted in the editor for performance reasons. This was discussed during rendering meeting with Clay and QbieShay
Most of the local variables in this method can be `const`.

I agree that technically this only needs to be emitted in the editor, although performance shouldn't be a concern.
Emitting a signal to which nothing is connected is rather cheap.
The `changed` signal already deviates from its documented behavior in many cases (see https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-signal-changed) with many resources not emitting it at all and others for every property change. 
And emitting it only in the editor further fragments the signal's behavior across contexts, violating the principle of consistent API behavior between editor and runtime. As @Mickeon pointed out, this would be the only situation where `changed` is exclusively emitted in the editor.
Not sure what the best solution is, but maybe using another signal (like the one you used further down below, `emission_shape_changed`) would be best to clearly separate it from the `changed` signal.
Probably an oversight, should be made consistent with the other code.
